content.tex: Section A
Investigation Eisenstein triples
You are advised to spend no more than 45 minutes on this section.
In this investigation you will look at the lengths of the sides of a triangle where one angle is \(60^{\circ}.\)
In the triangle:

\(\bullet\) the length of the shortest side is a centimetres \(\bullet\) the length of the longest side is \(b\) centimetres \(\bullet\) the length of the side opposite the \(60^{\circ}\) angle is \(c\) centimetres.
When a, \(b\) and \(c\) are integers the sides of the triangle make an Eisenstein triple \((a,\) b, \(c).\)
The cosine rule says that \(c^{2} = a^{2} +b^{2} -2ab\cos C\) . For an Eisenstein triple angle \(C = 60^{\circ}.\)
Give a reason why \(c^{2} = a^{2} +b^{2} -ab\) for an Eisenstein triple.
